policies.title: Privacy Policy
policies.text:
FoodSafe Manila - Private Testing Privacy Policy

This general notice describes the private testing build. Use fictional report
details. Real contact details and location still identify testers. This notice
does not claim institutional or legal certification.

1. Who Handles Your Data

The test is arranged by the FoodSafe Manila development/testing team that provided
your access. Contact the organizer through the channel used to arrange testing
with privacy questions or requests. No affiliation with a government agency or
university is implied by this general test notice.

2. Account and Contact Information

The service stores the name you provide, mobile number, password hash, and any
recovery email you provide. This supports test accounts, authentication, and account
recovery. Use a test display name where the organizer permits it. A working number
that you control is needed to test SMS OTP delivery. Your number and verification
message are sent to Semaphore; recovery emails are sent through Brevo.

The backend records your account ID, accepted Terms version, acknowledged Privacy
Policy version, and server timestamp. Privacy acknowledgement records that the
notice was acknowledged; it is not blanket consent to every use of your data.

3. Simulated Reports and Symptoms

For this trial, enter simulated symptoms and fictional food/exposure descriptions,
not genuine health information. Reports contain these test entries, report dates,
your account reference, and geographic data. They support testing submission,
review, investigation workflows, and aggregated analytics. Even a fictional report
can identify a tester when linked to an account or precise coordinates.

Do not include information about other people. Collection of genuine health data
is outside this private trial notice and requires a reviewed lawful basis and revised
disclosure before it starts.

4. Precise and Geographic Location

If you choose location features, the app reads device coordinates to identify a
district/barangay and provide nearby information. Submitting a test report sends
coordinates and geographic details to the backend. Location is optional for other
browsing; the current geographic report workflow requires it. You may skip that
test activity. Address lookup may use platform geocoding services, and map tiles
are loaded from OpenStreetMap.

When phone location permission is granted and location services are enabled, the
app automatically displays your location on location-based screens. There is no
separate in-app location toggle. OS permission is not acceptance of this Policy.
Revoke device permission in your phone settings to stop future location reads.
This does not automatically delete coordinates in existing reports.

5. Purposes, Lawful Bases, and Recipients

The trial purposes are account access/recovery, feature and usability testing,
debugging, and evaluating simulated reporting and analytics. Account details are
used to provide the requested testing account. Location and simulated report
processing are separately optional and requested through explicit controls.
The backend stores account and report records in MongoDB. Configured hosting and
delivery providers may process data outside the Philippines; ask the organizer
for the current deployment/provider details. Authorized testing staff can access
test records through the backend's role-controlled interfaces.
Agreement to Terms is not consent to unrelated processing.
No marketing or unrelated research consent is requested by these screens.

6. Retention and Your Choices

The testing period is the period arranged with your test organizer. The application
does not currently implement automatic deletion of account or report records.
Records remain stored until the organizer deletes them. Ask the organizer about
retention and backups before providing real personal information, and request
deletion through your agreed testing contact channel. No specific deletion deadline
is promised by this general notice.

Contact the test organizer to request information, access, correction,
objection, or erasure/blocking as applicable under Philippine privacy law. Where
processing relies on consent, use the same channel to withdraw it. The organizer
must explain applicable limits and the effect on testing features. Signing out
or stopping testing does not itself erase stored records.

7. Changes

The app displays this notice's version. The organizer must explain significant
changes before new processing, and obtain fresh acknowledgement or consent when
required. Existing acceptance evidence remains stored until the organizer deletes
it. An updated notice does not retroactively authorize a new
purpose for previously collected data.

8. Private Testing Scope

Do not submit genuine health reports or another person's personal information.
Ask the organizer before involving minors or extending the trial to real health
data. This general testing notice does not claim institutional or National Privacy
Commission approval and should be replaced with an operator-specific policy
before any broader deployment.

policies.title: Terms of Use
policies.text:
FoodSafe Manila - Private Testing Terms of Use

These general Terms cover a private testing trial, not a public release or an
official health service. They are not a claim of institutional or legal approval.

1. Test Organizer and Scope

The organizer is the FoodSafe Manila development/testing team that provided your
test access. Contact them through the channel used to arrange your testing.
Use this test build only with the organizer's
permission and for the agreed testing activities. Access to a test build does
not authorize distribution of accounts, credentials, or identifiable test data.

2. Nature of the Application

FoodSafe Manila is being evaluated for functionality, usability, and reliability.
Its maps, analytics, predictions, and reports may contain incomplete, simulated,
or inaccurate information. They must not be used to diagnose an illness, choose
treatment, decide whether food is safe, or replace professional advice. For an
actual health concern, use an appropriate healthcare or emergency service.

3. Accounts and Security

Provide a mobile number that you control when testing SMS verification. Keep your
password and verification codes private. Do not use another person's account,
impersonate another person, bypass access controls, or attempt unauthorized access.
Use a password created for this test rather than one used for another service.
Notify the organizer of suspected unauthorized access.

4. Test Reports and Feedback

Use simulated symptoms, food sources, and exposure descriptions for test reports.
Do not submit real medical histories, genuine health reports, or personal details
about other people. Do not enter names or contact details in free-text report
fields. If genuine health-data collection is needed later, the organizer must
provide a revised notice and establish its lawful basis before that activity.

Share bugs and usability feedback through the organizer's agreed channel. Avoid
including passwords, verification codes, or other people's personal information
in screenshots, recordings, or feedback.

5. Location and Privacy Choices

Read the separate Privacy Policy and the notice shown before reporting or using
location. Location is optional for browsing public information; the current report
feature requires location to test its geographic workflow. You may decline that
feature and continue other testing. Device permission is separate from Terms
acceptance, Privacy Policy acknowledgement, and purpose-specific consent.

6. Limitations and End of Testing

Features may fail or change during the trial. The organizer may pause testing or
restrict test access for security or operational reasons. Do not rely on this
test build for time-critical information. Test participation does not guarantee
continued access or transfer of test accounts into a future release.

You may stop participating. Contact the organizer for data requests; stopping
use or signing out does not itself delete previously stored data. The applicable
retention and deletion arrangements are described in the Privacy Policy.

7. Changes and Acceptance

The application displays the version you accept and records acceptance with your
account and a server timestamp. Material changes require review and explicit
acceptance of the required version before account updates or report submission.
You may decline and continue viewing public information or stop testing.

Accepting these Terms does not give blanket consent to data processing, waive
statutory rights, or substitute for separate optional choices. Any purpose-specific
consent must be explained and requested separately.

8. Questions

Contact the test organizer through your agreed testing channel about the trial,
these Terms, or an account issue. These general Terms are intended for private testing;
they do not claim approval by the National Privacy Commission or any institution.

policies.title: Before You Report
policies.text:
Reporting Disclosure for Private Testing

1. What the report contains

Use simulated symptoms and fictional suspected food/source and exposure details in this private trial. Do not enter genuine health information or another person's personal details. A report includes symptoms, food/source and exposure descriptions, report and submission dates, case count, your account reference, district/barangay, and precise device coordinates. Staff review may add investigation, classification, and surveillance-related fields. Even fictional entries may identify a tester when linked to an account or location.

2. Purpose and use

Reports support testing submission, review, investigation, geographic workflows, and aggregated report analytics. Citizen reports are kept separate from official case datasets; submitting a report does not automatically include it in official surveillance totals, outbreak thresholds, or prediction training. The app also displays analytics and predictions from backend datasets, which may contain simulated or incomplete information in this trial. Do not use this test app for diagnosis, treatment, or emergency decisions.

3. Access and recipients

Authorized testing staff may access reports through role-controlled backend interfaces. Reports are stored in MongoDB on the configured hosting infrastructure. Address lookup may use platform geocoding services and map tiles are loaded from OpenStreetMap. These services may process location or network information. Ask your test organizer for current hosting/provider details and any processing outside the Philippines. No government or institutional affiliation is implied.

4. Retention and choices

The testing period is arranged with your organizer. Automatic deletion of accounts and reports is not currently implemented; records remain until the organizer deletes them. Ask about retention and backups before providing identifiable information. Contact the organizer through your agreed testing channel for access, correction, deletion, or withdrawal of reporting consent. Signing out, stopping testing, or disabling location does not delete existing reports.

5. Separate reporting consent

Reporting is optional. Terms acceptance and Privacy Policy acknowledgement do not give consent to reporting or location processing. The controls below record acknowledgement of the reporting and location disclosures and purpose-specific consent for the simulated report, account reference, and precise location. Android or iOS controls device location access; there is no separate in-app location toggle or checkbox. When phone permission is granted and location services are enabled, the app automatically displays your location. You may decline and continue using other features.

Your reporting acknowledgement/consent version, location notice version, and server timestamp are saved with your account and referenced on submitted reports. Once accepted, this disclosure applies to later reports under the same versions; it is shown for acceptance again when the disclosure or applicable processing changes. Review the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy for the wider account and testing context.

policies.title: Before Using Location
policies.text:
Using location reads precise device coordinates to identify your district/barangay and provide nearby information during private testing. Reports send precise coordinates to the backend. Address lookup may use platform geocoding services; map tiles are requested from OpenStreetMap.

Location is optional for browsing public information. Continuing to device permission is separate from acknowledging the Privacy Policy or accepting Terms. Once phone permission is granted and location services are enabled, location-based screens automatically display your location. There is no separate in-app location toggle. You can decline or revoke permission in your phone settings. This stops future location reads, but does not delete coordinates in existing test reports. Contact the test organizer about those records.
